courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.contribution: Mandatory first-year formation.

courses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
courses.contribution: provides research design, operationalisation, sampling and statistical foundations for empirical inquiry

courses.name: Law, Society & Justice
courses.contribution: provides legal, socio-legal and normative foundations for analysing institutions, citizenship, rights and justice

courses.name: Modern History
courses.contribution: provides modern historical context for industrialisation, political ideologies, conflict, social change and the post-1945 order

courses.name: Histories of Gender
courses.contribution: studies nineteenth- to twenty-first-century American histories through gender, slavery, identity and social experience

courses.name: History of Empires
courses.contribution: Complementary global-historical framework: theories and comparative histories of empires and great-power politics support interpretation of United States global influence; no dedicated US-empire syllabus is claimed.

courses.name: Native American Histories
courses.contribution: directly studies Native American histories, settler colonialism, Indigenous experience and cultural survival

courses.name: History Research Seminar
courses.contribution: Complementary primary-source method: a course-filling paper uses diaries, letters and reports about the 1809  Walcheren expedition. This fixed European case teaches historical source analysis; it does not offer unrestricted American-history topic choice or replace a separate bachelor thesis.

courses.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
courses.contribution: examines the legal, historical and philosophical foundations of rights and their institutional protection

courses.name: Introduction to Public International Law
courses.contribution: provides the public-international-law framework for interstate relations, international organisations and global order

courses.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
courses.contribution: Complementary institutional analysis: compares constitutional and administrative principles in five legal systems, addressing government powers, democracy and rights. The workbook does not identify the five systems; dedicated US constitutional coverage is not assumed.

courses.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
courses.contribution: provides concepts of liberty, equality, authority, democracy and political obligation for analysing American political ideas

courses.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
courses.contribution: provides comparative tools for analysing political systems, institutions, parties, voters and democratic dissatisfaction

courses.name: Theory of International Relations
courses.contribution: develops historical and theoretical analysis of international relations, geopolitics, power and global institutions

courses.name: Peace & Conflict
courses.contribution: examines causes and consequences of violent and non-violent conflict and strategies for peace across political and social contexts

courses.name: Introduction to Sociology
courses.contribution: provides concepts and theories for analysing institutions, inequality, identities and social relations

courses.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courses.contribution: provides qualitative research design and interpretive methods for investigating culture, identity and social experience

courses.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
courses.contribution: develops social-movement theory through feminist, anti-colonial and environmental-justice cases

courses.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
courses.contribution: develops advanced social theory on civil society, solidarity, trust, the public and contemporary social change

courses.name: Psycholinguistics
courses.contribution: examines language processing and acquisition through psychology, linguistics and neuroscience

courses.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courses.contribution: provides cognitive and behavioural foundations for understanding language, thought and communication before advanced psycholinguistics

courses.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
courses.contribution: Complementary social-conflict application: an international youth-radicalisation project develops evidence-based educational materials about democratic culture, empathy and civic engagement; it is not a course on American extremism.

courses.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
courses.contribution: develops evidence-based written and spoken argument, rhetorical analysis and audience-aware communication

courses.name: Style & Meaning
courses.contribution: uses stylistics and linguistics to analyse how textual choices create meaning

courses.name: Persuasive Communication
courses.contribution: examines persuasion, framing, influence and communication ethics in public discourse

courses.name: Creative Communication Laboratory
courses.contribution: Direct cultural practice and analysis: poetry, performance, sound and hybrid creative projects examine linguistic and cultural meaning; it does not include singing, songwriting or music performance.

courses.name: Introduction to Western Art History
courses.contribution: provides historical and analytical foundations for studying art movements and institutions in Europe and the Americas

courses.name: Modern Art & Modern Museums
courses.contribution: examines modern art, museums and exhibitions and how institutions shape public interpretations of culture

courses.name: Writing Art's Histories
courses.contribution: Complementary historiography: examines how art historians from the sixteenth century onward have interpreted art through debates about aesthetics, authorship, identity and global art history; no independent art-research project is promised.

courses.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
courses.contribution: develops practical criticism across fiction, poetry, drama, non-fiction and film narrative

courses.name: Great Literary Works
courses.contribution: provides a chronological literary foundation and critical vocabulary for interpreting texts in historical and cultural context

courses.name: Life & Travel Writing
courses.contribution: examines memory, identity and self-representation across literary and popular-cultural life narratives

courses.name: Film & Text
courses.contribution: examines relations between literary and film narratives, including adaptation, intertextuality and cross-cultural interpretation

courses.name: Perspectives on Literary Meaning
courses.contribution: applies feminist, Marxist, cultural-minority, psychoanalytic and humanist perspectives in an independent literary research project

courses.name: Introduction to Film & Media
courses.contribution: provides foundations for analysing film and media as cultural forms that shape identity, representation and power

courses.name: Media Archaeology
courses.contribution: studies how media technologies shape the production, circulation and preservation of cultural meaning

courses.name: From T.V. to TikTok
courses.contribution: examines American social history and everyday life through mainstream media from the mid-twentieth century to the present

courses.name: Media & the Environment
courses.contribution: Complementary media application: analyses environmental representation using Anthropocene, animal, Indigenous and postcolonial perspectives. It supplies a specific ecological-cultural lens, rather than a general Indigenous-media syllabus.

courses.name: Media & Race
courses.contribution: directly studies race, systemic racism, resistance and cultural expression in American history and life

courses.name: The Documentary
courses.contribution: combines documentary history and analysis with production of a research-informed documentary

programmeComparability: Under theCP119 challenge, four directly American-focused courses (30EC) in the broad/political designs anchor coherent comparative history, politics, culture and social inquiry; cultural route has22.5EC directly American-focused work plus substantial literature/media study. These are qualified responses to a multidomain degree, not generic coherent programmes relabelledAmerican. Linguistics/proficiency/USliterature-survey gaps remain substantial and explicit.
retentionJudgment: Retain all40distinct courses: their direct or specific complementary roles support the concepts. The fixed European historical-source seminar is retained only as complementary primary-source methodology, not unrestrictedAmerican research. Art historiography, environmental representation and the youth project have bounded, accurate contributions. No weak additional programme is manufactured.
alignmentReview: All25external components and all72UCR placements inspected. Meaningful partial correspondences retained, dedicated phonetics/proficiency/literature and philosophy gaps remain blank; constitutional comparison explicitly lacks confirmedUScoverage. Thesis stays external with optional research separate. No credit equivalence is implied.
